outcomeNote: A mishna stating a rule with its prooftext; no named parties and no dispute.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ נָפְלָה סַכִּין וְשָׁחֲטָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשָּׁחֲטָה כְּדַרְכָּהּ – פְּסוּלָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְזָבַחְתָּ … וְאָכַלְתָּ״, מַה שֶּׁאַתָּה זוֹבֵחַ אַתָּה אוֹכֵל.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» If «a knife fell and slaughtered» an animal, «although» the knife «slaughtered» the animal «in the standard manner,» the slaughter is «not valid, as it is stated: “And you shall slaughter…and you shall eat”» (Deuteronomy 27:7), from which it is derived: «That which you slaughter you may eat,» and that which was slaughtered on its own, you may not eat.

moves.summary: a knife that fell and slaughtered renders the slaughter invalid even if it cut in the standard manner
moves.about: the prooftext that only what you slaughter may be eaten

moves.summary: the ruling is grounded in 'and you shall slaughter and you shall eat' — what you slaughter you may eat
moves.about: the verse's sequence teaches that only an animal you actively slaughter may be eaten, excluding one slaughtered by a falling knife
